record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Xie and Yau conjectured that every three-dimensional canonical singularity gives rise to a 5d N = 1 superconformal field theory. Does M-theory on any 3d canonical singularity always define a 5d N = 1 SCFT, and can tools such as dot diagrams and magnetic quivers be used to verify this conjecture?

evidence.quote: Question 6. Does M-theory on any 3d canonical singularity always define a 5d N = 1 SCFT (conjecture 1 in [45])? Can we use the tools including dot diagrams and magnetic quivers to verify this conjecture?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In M-theory, compactification on a local Calabi–Yau threefold with an isolated singularity is expected to engineer a five-dimensional superconformal field theory (5d N=1 SCFT) at the origin of its Coulomb branch. A normal complex threefold singularity (X,0) is called canonical if, for some (equivalently any) resolution π: Y → X with exceptional divisors E_i, one has K_Y = π* K_X + Σ a_i E_i with a_i ≥ 0. Among the structural data attached to a 5d N=1 SCFT one has its Coulomb branch (with prepotential determined by triple intersection numbers on a crepant resolution), its flavor symmetry (read off from the singularity type along the one-dimensional singular locus), and combinatorial/representation-theoretic descriptions such as "dot diagrams" and "magnetic quivers" that compute, for instance, the Higgs branch.

Conjecture (to be assessed). Every three-dimensional canonical singularity (X,0), viewed as a local Calabi–Yau threefold, defines via M-theory a five-dimensional N=1 superconformal field theory.

Problem. Prove or disprove the above conjecture. Equivalently, determine whether for every three-dimensional canonical singularity the M-theory compactification on (X,0) yields an interacting 5d N=1 SCFT, and develop systematic tools — in particular dot diagrams associated with the singularity and magnetic quivers describing the Higgs branch — that allow one to verify the existence of such an SCFT and to compute its physical invariants (Coulomb branch dimension, prepotential, flavor symmetry, Higgs branch) directly from the geometry of the canonical singularity.
artifact.status_search_result: The Xie–Yau conjecture (every 3d canonical singularity yields a 5d N=1 SCFT via M-theory) remains an active research program. Subsequent works (e.g., Closset–Del Zotto–Saxena 2020/2021, Closset–Schäfer-Nameki–Wang 2022, and 2024 papers on isolated complete intersection singularities) have verified it in broad classes of cases (toric, hypersurface, ICIS) and developed magnetic-quiver/dot-diagram techniques, but no complete proof for all 3d canonical singularities is known.

status_evidence.title: Three dimensional canonical singularity and five dimensional N=1 SCFT (Xie–Yau)
status_evidence.snippet: We conjecture that every three dimensional canonical singularity defines a five dimensional N=1 SCFT.

status_evidence.title: Coulomb and Higgs branches from canonical singularities, Part I
status_evidence.snippet: Studies 5d SCFTs from hypersurface canonical singularities with smooth Calabi–Yau resolutions, computing Coulomb and Higgs branches.
status_evidence.claim: Partial verification in classes of canonical singularities, indicating the conjecture is still being tested case by case.

status_evidence.title: 5d SCFTs from isolated complete intersection singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the geometric engineering dictionary to ICIS canonical singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work extending verification, indicating the general conjecture is not yet fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: 5d and 4d SCFTs: canonical singularities, trinions and S-dualities
status_evidence.snippet: Develops tools to associate 5d SCFTs to canonical threefold singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Active development of tools relevant to the conjecture.
